problem: E11's Experience Index Guard and E25's Pointer Guard shared the same real concept (CURRENT/STALE, missing/current target, cached-vs-live mismatch) but returned differently-shaped results -- no common reporting layer existed.

decision.decision_summary: Defined a 6-field CurrencyContract, adapted (never re-derived) both real guards' outputs into it, applied the unified layer once to both real subjects (Experience Index: STALE, expected; PB pointer: CURRENT), and generated exactly 1 CANDIDATE_ONLY refresh candidate for the STALE subject via a single unified generator.

action.action_summary: Implemented CurrencyContract + 2 adapters + 1 unified refresh-candidate generator. Reused currencyGuard() (E11) and pointerCurrencyGuard() (E25) verbatim, 0 verdict logic changed. Applied once to real data; verified adapters via 3 synthetic-fixture tests.

result.note: Adds a reporting-layer integration; does not change either Guard's verdict logic, does not refresh the Index or the pointer, does not change this Goal's own real status.

cause.root_cause_summary: 2 real, independently-built Guards (E11, E25) converged on the same underlying concept without ever being connected by a shared contract -- future consumers would have had to know 2 different result shapes for the same idea.

lesson: Integration does not require building a 3rd mechanism -- a thin adapter layer that reshapes 2 already-correct, already-verified real outputs into 1 common contract achieves the stated goal without touching (and therefore without risking) either original Guard's real, hard-won correctness.
